source.title: Rethinking Generalization in Knowledge Graph Embedding: An Empirical Study and Sparse Peak Regularization
source.authors: Lin-Yu Li; Zhi Jin; Yuan-Peng He; Dong-Ming Jin; Hao-Ran Duan; Zheng-Wei Tao; Xuan Zhang; Jian-Dong Li; Huan-Yao Zhang; Gadeng Luosang; Nyima Tashi

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices. Some equations and tables are flattened, but the relevant values are assignable from their layout.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether regularization changes generalization in knowledge graph embedding models, extending the topic to a different task and model family.
record.gate_note: The study measures training–validation or training–test gaps and reports held-out link-prediction results with and without regularization. It does not test random-label memorization, natural-label classification, width scaling, architecture comparisons between convolutional and fully connected image classifiers, optimizer choice, or batch size.
record.test_reason: The study measures regularization effects on knowledge-graph link prediction, which none of V1–V8 specifies. Its Dropout comparisons use graph neural link-prediction models and ranking metrics, rather than the fully connected or convolutional classifiers named in V6. Generalization gaps alone do not test V1 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the evaluated KGE settings. The authors also conclude that their proposed SPR achieves the best results in nearly all tested settings relative to existing regularizers. For HGE, the unregularized baseline still retains temporal regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates link prediction on knowledge graphs, with different model families, datasets, metrics, and regularization methods from the claim versions' image-classification and language-model settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization strength and SPR threshold δ affect performance; the text reports non-monotonic sensitivity to the regularization rate and threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularization narrows held-out generalization gaps in static, temporal, and multimodal KGE models; OTKGE's final MRR gap falls from 0.234 to 0.089 with N3 and 0.077 with SPR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable regularization can reduce overfitting in knowledge-graph embedding models.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout raises FB15K-237 test MRR from 0.216 to 0.333 for CompGCN-T and from 0.302 to 0.352 for CompGCN-C.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can improve held-out link-prediction rankings in graph neural knowledge-graph models.

fits_no_version.finding: SPR improves test link-prediction MRR over unregularized KGE baselines in the recorded comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective penalties on high-energy embedding components can improve KGE link prediction.

record.problems: Hyperparameters were obtained from a partial parameter search. The reported results are averaged over three runs, but no error bars or uncertainty estimates are given. Some figure findings are only described qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Table 1 and Table 2 contain many additional regularizer-by-backbone-by-dataset metric results; representative MRR comparisons are retained, while the remaining metric-specific table entries are omitted because the catalog claim versions do not specify KGE link-prediction metrics. Figure 5 and Figure 6 threshold/rate sweeps are not separately rowed because these measure SPR hyperparameter sensitivity, not a mapped claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in the specified fully connected and convolutional classifiers, including small-data, excessive-dropout, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the reported KGE improvements. The record incorrectly says Dropout results lack numerical prose: Appendix A.1 explicitly supplies R7–R8. No additional results bearing on a listed version are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label classification generalization.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and tuning choices.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.

The paper reports Dropout results for CompGCN in Figure 6, but the figure values are not described numerically in text; it does not test the stated classifier regimes or small-data and augmentation qualifications.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting held-out accuracy.
